result.markdown: --- title: "Forecasting Seoul's hourly bike demand" subtitle: "A self-contained tidyverse and tidymodels case study" author: "Miguelangel Palma Rojas" date: last-modified lang: en description: "Visible, end-to-end forecasting code for bicycle operations, evaluated on a strictly future holdout." --- Hourly demand is not just a prediction problem. It is an operating decision: how many bicycles should be available, where should the team expect pressure, and how much uncertainty remains at commuter peaks? This notebook is intentionally self-contained. Every transformation, split, model, metric, and chart used below is written here and executed from top to bottom. ## Packages and reproducibility ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(tidymodels) library(ranger) library(knitr) tidymodels_prefer() set.seed(2026) ``` ::: ## Data contract and quality The governed snapshot contains one row per date and hour. Before modeling, the notebook verifies the complete schema, missingness, physical ranges, nonnegative rentals, and unique date-hour keys. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} required_columns <- c( "date", "rented_bike_count", "hour", "temperature_c", "humidity_pct", "wind_speed_ms", "visibility_10m", "dew_point_c", "solar_radiation_mj_m2", "rainfall_mm", "snowfall_cm", "season", "holiday", "functioning_day", "weekday", "is_weekend" ) bikes <- read_csv( "data/seoul_bike_snapshot.csv", show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(date = col_date()) ) |> mutate( weekday = factor( weekday, levels = c( "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday" ) ), across(c(season, holiday, functioning_day, is_weekend), factor) ) |> arrange(date, hour) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} stopifnot( setequal(names(bikes), required_columns), !anyNA(bikes), all(bikes$rented_bike_count >= 0), all(bikes$hour %in% 0:23), between(min(bikes$humidity_pct), 0, 100), between(max(bikes$humidity_pct), 0, 100), nrow(distinct(bikes, date, hour)) == nrow(bikes) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data_profile <- bikes |> summarise( observations = n(), first_date = min(date), last_date = max(date), operating_days = n_distinct(date[functioning_day == "Yes"]), closure_hours = sum(functioning_day == "No"), average_hourly_demand = mean(rented_bike_count), peak_hourly_demand = max(rented_bike_count), missing_cells = sum(is.na(pick(everything()))) ) data_profile |> kable(digits = 1, caption = "Validated snapshot profile") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Validated snapshot profile | observations|first_date |last_date | operating_days| closure_hours| average_hourly_demand| peak_hourly_demand| missing_cells| |------------:|:----------|:----------|--------------:|-------------:|---------------------:|------------------:|-------------:| | 8760|2017-12-01 |2018-11-30 | 353| 295| 704.6| 3556| 0| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bikes |> filter(functioning_day == "Yes") |> summarise( average_demand = mean(rented_bike_count), .by = c(weekday, hour) ) |> ggplot(aes(hour, weekday, fill = average_demand)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) + labs( title = "Commute peaks define the operating rhythm", x = "Hour", y = "Weekday", fill = "Average rentals" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Average operating-day rentals by weekday and hour.](index_files/figure-html/demand-rhythm-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Feature engineering and future holdout Closures are handled as a service-status rule, not learned as zero demand. The latest 20% of complete dates is reserved untouched for final evaluation. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} origin_date <- min(bikes$date) model_data <- bikes |> filter(functioning_day == "Yes") |> transmute( date, rented_bike_count, hour = factor(hour, levels = 0:23), weekday, month = factor(format(date, "%m"), levels = sprintf("%02d", 1:12)), season, holiday, is_weekend, trend_day = as.numeric(date - origin_date), temperature_c, humidity_pct, wind_speed_ms, visibility_10m, dew_point_c, solar_radiation_mj_m2, rainfall_mm, snowfall_cm ) |> arrange(date, hour) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} test_days <- ceiling(n_distinct(model_data$date) * 0.20) first_test_date <- model_data |> distinct(date) |> arrange(desc(date)) |> slice_head(n = test_days) |> summarise(first_test_date = min(date)) |> pull(first_test_date) training_data <- model_data |> filter(date < first_test_date) testing_data <- model_data |> filter(date >= first_test_date) tibble( sample = c("Training", "Future holdout"), first_date = c(min(training_data$date), min(testing_data$date)), last_date = c(max(training_data$date), max(testing_data$date)), observations = c(nrow(training_data), nrow(testing_data)) ) |> kable(caption = "Chronological final split") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Chronological final split |sample |first_date |last_date | observations| |:--------------|:----------|:----------|------------:| |Training |2017-12-01 |2018-09-10 | 6768| |Future holdout |2018-09-11 |2018-11-30 | 1697| ::: ::: ## Expanding temporal validation Hyperparameters are selected only inside the training period. Each 28-day validation window follows an expanding training window and a one-day gap. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} training_dates <- training_data |> distinct(date) |> arrange(date) |> pull(date) assessment_days <- 28L gap_days <- 1L analysis_ends <- round(seq( floor(length(training_dates) * 0.45), length(training_dates) - assessment_days - gap_days, length.out = 4 )) |> as.integer() assessment_starts <- analysis_ends + gap_days + 1L assessment_ends <- assessment_starts + assessment_days - 1L ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} split_01 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[1]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[1]]:assessment_ends[[1]]]) ), training_data ) split_02 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[2]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[2]]:assessment_ends[[2]]]) ), training_data ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} split_03 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[3]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[3]]:assessment_ends[[3]]]) ), training_data ) split_04 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[4]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[4]]:assessment_ends[[4]]]) ), training_data ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} temporal_splits <- list(split_01, split_02, split_03, split_04) temporal_resamples <- manual_rset( temporal_splits, paste0("Window", str_pad(seq_along(temporal_splits), 2, pad = "0")) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} window_summary <- tibble( window = temporal_resamples$id, training_start = c( min(analysis(split_01)$date), min(analysis(split_02)$date), min(analysis(split_03)$date), min(analysis(split_04)$date) ), training_end = c( max(analysis(split_01)$date), max(analysis(split_02)$date), max(analysis(split_03)$date), max(analysis(split_04)$date) ), validation_start = c( min(assessment(split_01)$date), min(assessment(split_02)$date), min(assessment(split_03)$date), min(assessment(split_04)$date) ), validation_end = c( max(assessment(split_01)$date), max(assessment(split_02)$date), max(assessment(split_03)$date), max(assessment(split_04)$date) ) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} window_summary <- window_summary |> mutate( training_rows = c( nrow(analysis(split_01)), nrow(analysis(split_02)), nrow(analysis(split_03)), nrow(analysis(split_04)) ), validation_rows = c( nrow(assessment(split_01)), nrow(assessment(split_02)), nrow(assessment(split_03)), nrow(assessment(split_04)) ) ) window_summary |> kable(caption = "Expanding validation windows") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Expanding validation windows |window |training_start |training_end |validation_start |validation_end | training_rows| validation_rows| |:--------|:--------------|:------------|:----------------|:--------------|-------------:|---------------:| |Window01 |2017-12-01 |2018-04-05 |2018-04-07 |2018-05-05 | 3024| 672| |Window02 |2017-12-01 |2018-05-19 |2018-05-21 |2018-06-17 | 4032| 672| |Window03 |2017-12-01 |2018-07-01 |2018-07-03 |2018-07-30 | 5064| 672| |Window04 |2017-12-01 |2018-08-12 |2018-08-14 |2018-09-10 | 6072| 672| ::: ::: ## Preprocessing and model specifications The recipe identifies the date, encodes categorical calendar signals, removes zero-variance and linearly dependent columns, and normalizes numeric predictors. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bike_recipe <- recipe(rented_bike_count ~ ., data = training_data) |> update_role(date, new_role = "id") |> step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |> step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |> step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |> step_zv(all_predictors()) |> step_lincomb(all_numeric_predictors()) |> step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) ``` ::: ### Linear regression ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} linear_workflow <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bike_recipe) |> add_model(linear_reg() |> set_engine("lm")) ``` ::: ### Elastic Net ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} elastic_workflow <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bike_recipe) |> add_model( linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) |> set_engine("glmnet") ) ``` ::: ### Random forest ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} forest_workflow <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bike_recipe) |> add_model( rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 300) |> set_engine( "ranger", importance = "permutation", num.threads = 1, seed = 2029 ) |> set_mode("regression") ) ``` ::: Only the source code is shown here. The verbose internal printout of the recipe and workflow is intentionally suppressed because it adds no analytical value. ## Tuning and final fits ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tuning_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, mae) ``` ::: ### Elastic Net tuning ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2027) elastic_grid <- grid_space_filling( penalty(range = c(-5, 0)), mixture(), size = 6 ) elastic_tuning <- tune_grid( elastic_workflow, resamples = temporal_resamples, grid = elastic_grid, metrics = tuning_metrics, control = control_grid(allow_par = FALSE) ) best_elastic <- select_best(elastic_tuning, metric = "rmse") ``` ::: ### Random forest tuning ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2028) forest_grid <- grid_space_filling( mtry(range = c(4L, 18L)), min_n(range = c(5L, 40L)), size = 6 ) forest_tuning <- tune_grid( forest_workflow, resamples = temporal_resamples, grid = forest_grid, metrics = tuning_metrics, control = control_grid(allow_par = FALSE) ) best_forest <- select_best(forest_tuning, metric = "rmse") ``` ::: ### Final model fits ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} linear_fit <- fit(linear_workflow, training_data) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} elastic_fit <- elastic_workflow |> finalize_workflow(best_elastic) |> fit(training_data) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2029) forest_fit <- forest_workflow |> finalize_workflow(best_forest) |> fit(training_data) ``` ::: ## Final holdout results The benchmark averages historical demand by weekday and hour. If a combination is unavailable, it falls back to the hourly and then global training mean. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} calendar_average <- training_data |> summarise(calendar_average = mean(rented_bike_count), .by = c(hour, weekday)) hourly_average <- training_data |> summarise(hour_average = mean(rented_bike_count), .by = hour) calendar_predictions <- testing_data |> left_join(calendar_average, by = c("hour", "weekday")) |> left_join(hourly_average, by = "hour") |> transmute( date, hour, rented_bike_count, .pred = coalesce( calendar_average, hour_average, mean(training_data$rented_bike_count) ), model = "Calendar baseline" ) ``` ::: ### Linear regression predictions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} linear_predictions <- testing_data |> select(date, hour, rented_bike_count) |> bind_cols(predict(linear_fit, new_data = testing_data)) |> mutate(.pred = pmax(0, .pred), model = "Linear regression") ``` ::: ### Elastic Net predictions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} elastic_predictions <- testing_data |> select(date, hour, rented_bike_count) |> bind_cols(predict(elastic_fit, new_data = testing_data)) |> mutate(.pred = pmax(0, .pred), model = "Elastic Net") ``` ::: ### Random forest predictions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} forest_predictions <- testing_data |> select(date, hour, rented_bike_count) |> bind_cols(predict(forest_fit, new_data = testing_data)) |> mutate(.pred = pmax(0, .pred), model = "Random forest") ``` ::: ### Holdout metrics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predictions <- bind_rows( calendar_predictions, linear_predictions, elastic_predictions, forest_predictions ) peak_threshold <- quantile( training_data$rented_bike_count, probs = 0.90, names = FALSE ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model_metrics <- predictions |> summarise( rmse = sqrt(mean((rented_bike_count - .pred)^2)), mae = mean(abs(rented_bike_count - .pred)), rsq = rsq_trad_vec(rented_bike_count, .pred), wape_pct = 100 * sum(abs(rented_bike_count - .pred)) / sum(rented_bike_count), bias = mean(.pred - rented_bike_count), peak_mae = mean( abs(rented_bike_count[rented_bike_count >= peak_threshold] - .pred[rented_bike_count >= peak_threshold]) ), .by = model ) |> arrange(rmse) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} leader <- model_metrics |> slice_min(rmse, n = 1) baseline_rmse <- model_metrics |> filter(model == "Calendar baseline") |> pull(rmse) improvement <- 100 * (baseline_rmse - leader$rmse) / baseline_rmse model_metrics |> mutate( rmse = round(rmse, 1), mae = round(mae, 1), rsq = round(rsq, 1), wape_pct = round(wape_pct, 1), bias = round(bias, 1), peak_mae = round(peak_mae, 1) ) |> kable(caption = "Operational metrics on unseen future dates") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Operational metrics on unseen future dates |model | rmse| mae| rsq| wape_pct| bias| peak_mae| |:-----------------|-----:|-----:|---:|--------:|------:|--------:| |Random forest | 319.6| 225.9| 0.7| 25.2| -55.5| 564.0| |Elastic Net | 365.1| 268.6| 0.6| 30.0| -77.7| 713.6| |Linear regression | 414.0| 321.5| 0.5| 35.9| -204.1| 784.5| |Calendar baseline | 444.0| 323.7| 0.5| 36.2| -206.5| 866.4| ::: ::: ::: {.metric-grid} ::: {.metric-card} Random forest Best final model ::: ::: {.metric-card} 319.6 bikes Holdout RMSE ::: ::: {.metric-card} 28.0% RMSE gain vs calendar baseline ::: ::: {.metric-card} 564 bikes Peak-demand MAE ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## Decision takeaway Use the winning model as a planning signal, not an autonomous dispatch rule. It materially improves the calendar benchmark, but its negative bias and larger peak error call for an operational safety buffer. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model_metrics |> ggplot(aes(rmse, reorder(model, -rmse), fill = model)) + geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = 0.68) + geom_text(aes(label = round(rmse, 1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) + scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.85) + labs(title = "Final holdout error by model", x = "RMSE (bikes)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Lower RMSE is better; evaluation uses only the final future holdout.](index_files/figure-html/model-comparison-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Operational diagnostics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} winning_model <- leader$model[[1]] predictions |> filter(model == winning_model, date >= max(date) - 6) |> mutate(timestamp = as.POSIXct(date) + as.numeric(as.character(hour)) * 3600) |> select(timestamp, observed = rented_bike_count, predicted = .pred) |> pivot_longer(c(observed, predicted), names_to = "series", values_to = "bikes") |> ggplot(aes(timestamp, bikes, color = series)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.75) + scale_color_manual(values = c(observed = "#264653", predicted = "#E76F51")) + labs( title = str_c("Observed and predicted demand — ", winning_model), x = NULL, y = "Bikes", color = NULL ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Observed demand and the winning model over the final seven days.](index_files/figure-html/holdout-trace-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predictions |> filter(model == winning_model) |> mutate( hour = as.integer(as.character(hour)), residual = rented_bike_count - .pred, peak = rented_bike_count >= peak_threshold ) |> ggplot(aes(hour, residual, color = peak)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#6C757D") + geom_jitter(width = 0.18, alpha = 0.25) + geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "#E76F51") + scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#457B9D", `TRUE` = "#D62828")) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) + labs( title = "Peak-hour errors remain the hardest problem", x = "Hour", y = "Observed minus predicted", color = "Peak demand" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Positive residuals indicate under-forecasting.](index_files/figure-html/peak-errors-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} variable_importance <- forest_fit |> extract_fit_engine() |> pluck("variable.importance") |> enframe(name = "variable", value = "importance") |> arrange(desc(importance)) |> slice_head(n = 12) variable_importance |> ggplot(aes(importance, reorder(variable, importance))) + geom_col(fill = "#2A9D8F") + labs(title = "Random forest permutation importance", x = "Importance", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Permutation importance describes predictive contribution, not causality.](index_files/figure-html/feature-importance-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Temperature, trend, moisture conditions, solar radiation, and commute-hour indicators carry much of the signal. This does not make them causal levers; it makes them useful forecasting inputs. ## From forecast to action - Refresh the forecast before each operating shift with the latest weather outlook. - Convert expected rentals into station-level targets only after adding station inventory and trip-flow data. - Add a peak buffer when the cost of stockouts exceeds the cost of carrying idle bicycles. - Monitor WAPE, bias, and peak MAE by season; retrain when performance drifts beyond agreed thresholds. - Keep closures outside the demand model and handle them with an explicit service-status rule. The dataset covers one year and has no station, capacity, pricing, event, or forecast-weather fields. The result demonstrates sound model evaluation, but it is not yet a production rebalancing system. See the [methodology](docs/methodology.md), [model card](docs/model-card.md), and [data dictionary](docs/data-dictionary.md) for the complete audit trail.
